en.title: GTA 5's Trevor Actor Pitches Wild 'Toilet Scene' Cameo for GTA 6
en.summary: Steven Ogg, the iconic voice of Trevor Philips, has shared a darkly humorous vision for his character's potential return in Grand Theft Auto 6. He suggests a memorable, if brief, send-off for the volatile anti-hero.
en.body:
The sheer impact of **Trevor Philips** on the gaming landscape is undeniable. Portrayed with unhinged brilliance by **Steven Ogg**, the chaotic force of nature from **Grand Theft Auto 5** left an indelible mark. Now, Ogg himself has offered a creative, albeit characteristically bizarre, idea for how Trevor might make a fleeting appearance in **Grand Theft Auto 6**, the highly anticipated next installment from Rockstar Games.

Speaking with Principle Magazine, Ogg detailed a specific scenario he believes would serve as a fitting, albeit abrupt, farewell for Trevor. His vision involves the character appearing early in the game, engaged in a mundane yet inherently vulgar act: "sitting on the toilet." This moment, he feels, would serve as a symbolic "pass the torch" gesture, acknowledging the end of Trevor's story and paving the way for the new protagonists, **Lucia** and **Jason**, to claim the spotlight. Ogg pointed out the full-circle nature of such a scene, referencing Trevor's own explosive introduction in **GTA 5**, where he brutally attacks **Johnny Klebitz** from **Grand Theft Auto 4**.

> "I’d like to think that maybe he’s just sitting on the toilet or doing some weird thing, like walking around, and something falls on his head and knocks him out. It’s just like, ‘Okay, he’s done.’ He’s acknowledged, and now it’s time for the new people to come in."

Ogg expressed curiosity about how characters from **GTA 5** would look with the advancements in technology since its 2013 release, but he also voiced a general skepticism towards the constant demand for sequels and reboots, noting their financial drivers. He also took the opportunity to clarify his stance on **GTA** and his iconic character, pushing back against fan theories that suggest he dislikes the franchise or Trevor himself. Ogg stated he has always been proud of his work on **GTA 5** and what Rockstar created, despite not playing the game himself and finding it irksome when fans addressed him solely as Trevor in real life.

## The Fan Connection

For the legions of **Grand Theft Auto** fans eagerly awaiting **GTA 6**, any hint of continuity or connection to past beloved characters is a significant point of discussion. Trevor Philips, despite his reprehensible actions, became a fan favorite due to his unpredictable nature and **Ogg's** captivating performance. The idea of a cameo, especially one that acknowledges the passing of the torch, resonates with the community's desire for narrative cohesion and a sense of closure for established characters. While **Rockstar Games** has remained tight-lipped about specific character returns, the fan base is always looking for subtle nods or direct inclusions that bridge the gap between games.

## What's Next

Details regarding the full cast and narrative of **Grand Theft Auto 6** remain largely under wraps. **Rockstar Games** has not officially confirmed any appearances from **GTA 5** characters, including Trevor Philips. Players will have to wait for further official announcements or the game's eventual release to see if Ogg's imaginative send-off, or any other form of continuity, makes it into the final product.

content_raw: Steven Ogg famously portrayed the wildcard character Trevor in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 5, and he wishes Rockstar brought the character back for GTA 6 . Speaking to Principle Magazine , Ogg said it would have been a nice moment to "pass the torch" to have Trevor show up at the beginning of GTA 6 "sitting on the toilet" or doing some "weird thing" like walking around having something fall on his head, knocking him to the ground. In short, Ogg said he wanted Trevor to have some kind of "acknowledgement" that Trevor's story is over and it's time for Jason and Lucia to take center stage in GTA 6. Ogg said it could have been a nice full circle moment because, in GTA 5, Trevor's first scene shows him bashing Johnny Klebitz from GTA 4 . "I’m not a fan of all of the reboots and the sequels. I don’t get the … the hunger for that, but there is, because it makes money and that’s why people do it," he said. Ogg went on to say things have come so far since GTA 5, so he wanted to see how characters from GTA 5 could look in GTA 6, given the technical improvements from the past decade. "So, I’d be curious. But you know, not my duck, not my bottle. Not my monkey, not my cage," he said. Also in the interview, Ogg pushed back against the online theories that he is no fan of GTA and Trevor. He said he's always been proud of Trevor and proud of what Rockstar created. He doesn't play GTA 5, but he said people are out of line for taking his soundbites about GTA 5 and spinning them into a belief that he's no fan of GTA or his character. He acknowledged he didn't like how people would call him Trevor, and not Steven, in real life, though. "That’s been all blown out of proportion. Or that I hate GTA and now I’m starting to embrace it more. No, it’s just early on, there was a lot of people calling me Trevor. And I’d be like, 'Well, my name is Steven,'" he said. "So I could never understand that. So it’s always like 'What’s your name, David? Okay, Nolan.' It doesn’t make sense if you know someone’s name and you’re calling them someone else’s name. I don’t get it. And I understand people associate with characters and connections," he said. "At these Comic Cons, they’re not Documentary Cons. So I couldn’t be these people. I mean, I couldn’t even be Trevor, because he’s a cartoon. Simon [from The Walking Dead] was a human on a TV show, at least. Yeah, it’s just one of those things. It’s like… [scratches head]. It’s like me calling you, you know, Barbara." Trevor was one of the three playable characters in GTA 5, alongside Michael (Ned Luke) and Franklin (Shawn Fonteno). Ogg, in particular, landed some notable acting roles after GTA 5, appearing in the TV shows Better Call Saul, Snowpiercer, and Westworld, along with the films Emancipation and Unabomber. Trevor was apparently going to be in more content for GTA 5, as Ogg said Rockstar canceled Trevor-centric DLC that would have featured a James Bond-like story .
